html:
The Great Mosque of Damascus, built from 705 to 715 by the caliph al-Walid I, when Damascus was the capital of the Umayyad caliphate. It is one of the oldest and grandest mosques in the world.

The site had held a Roman temple of Jupiter and then a church of John the Baptist, whose head is said to rest in a shrine inside. Al-Walid built a huge prayer hall with three long aisles and a wide courtyard with arcades. Its walls were covered in gold glass mosaics of trees, rivers and fine buildings, with no people or animals, which many read as a picture of paradise. Craftsmen trained in the Byzantine tradition likely did the work.

Its plan of courtyard, long prayer hall and minarets became a model for mosques across the Islamic world. It survived fires, earthquakes and the sack of the city by Timur in 1401. Saladin is buried in a garden beside it. In 2001 Pope John Paul II visited, the first pope to enter a mosque.
sum: The Great Mosque of Damascus, built from 705 to 715 by the caliph al-Walid I, when Damascus was the capital of the Umayyad caliphate. It is one of the oldest and grandest mosques in the world.
